notes: Leaves out the most distinctive fact, that the tank was set up during a live session ('set trực tiếp trong một buổi live')
'đá xếp khéo' is a vague, praising phrase rather than a clear description; it could fit many Iwagumi pages
"lũa đơn" sounds stiff and compressed; the text says "một khúc lũa duy nhất", so "một khúc lũa" would read more naturally
"Bể bonsai lũa đơn vươn cao" piles nouns together, so it's unclear what "vươn cao" describes (the tank or the driftwood)
"với cát, đá và lũa" reads a bit like a translation; something like "Bể không cây phối màu cát, đá, lũa" would sound more natural
"Bể Diorama gờ đá" reads compressed; "Bể diorama với gờ đá…" would flow more naturally
"Diorama" capitalized mid-title; Vietnamese usage would normally lowercase the style name
"dốc đứng" goes a bit further than the text: the text calls the range "dãy núi dốc" and says only the back-right peak cluster is "gần như dựng đứng"
"Bể Iwagumi dãy núi đá Seiryu" strings nouns together with no linking word, so it reads choppy; something like "Bể Iwagumi dựng dãy núi dốc bằng đá Seiryu" would read more naturally
Name credit 'Chonlatee jaturonrusmee' leaves the surname lowercase; should be 'Jaturonrusmee'
'Bể Nature' mixes in English; 'Bể phong cách Nature' reads more naturally
'đàn rasbora' is close enough, but the text says 'các loài rasbora cỡ rất nhỏ', which means several species, not just one school
"Bể Nature cổ điển" is a bit clipped; "Bể phong cách Nature cổ điển" would read more naturally and match the text's "nature style kiểu cổ điển"
"lũa" alone doesn't set it apart from Guide 1, which also has dark driftwood, but "Cyperus helferi" does
Overlaps with Guide 1, which also has dark driftwood ('lũa sẫm') and plants that grow without CO2; only 'cây dễ trồng' vs 'Cyperus helferi' tells them apart
Leaves out the low-light angle ('ánh sáng yếu'), which would set this page apart more clearly
'Nature' comes from the source's title, not the page's text; acceptable, but the text never says 'Nature'
"Bể Nature rừng cây rậm" is clunky as a direct compound; something like "kiểu rừng rậm" would read more naturally
Hard to tell apart from Guide 1 ("Bể Nature cổ điển với lũa"), which also has driftwood, a dark substrate and a forest feel; "rậm" is the only real difference
"lũa trên nền tối" puts the weight on the driftwood, while the text stresses dense greenery against a dark background and substrate
"vòm lũa" narrows the arch to driftwood only; the text calls it "Bể hình vòm / cầu" and builds it from both lũa and đá
Saying "bể" three times ("Bể bờ ao, bể vòm lũa và bể cây bám") reads a little clunky
Leaves out the page's sections on maintenance and design approach, though listing the three tanks is still an accurate summary
"Diorama" is capitalized mid-title; the text writes "diorama" in lowercase, so the title should too
"Diorama" is capitalized mid-phrase, which looks a bit like a translation. "bể diorama" is more natural.
"rừng trên vách đá" is close to the text but slightly loose. The text says "mép vách đá có rừng phủ" (a forest-covered cliff edge).
"với lũa và Bucephalandra" picks out a minor planting detail. The page's main point, the depth illusion from big-to-small hardscape and plants front to back, is left out.
"đá sẫm màu và cây xanh rậm" is also true of Guide 1 (dark wood, black stones, dense green plants), so only "Iwagumi" sets this page apart
Leaves out the page's main point, that this is a lush variation ("biến tấu") on the plain classic Iwagumi style, and its warm, spring-like feel
"Bể Nature" mixes English into the Vietnamese; the text itself says "phong cách thiên nhiên". Fishkeepers do understand it, though.
"lũa sẫm cùng rêu và ráy anubias" is accurate but long. Guide 2 also features driftwood ("lũa"), so the moss and anubias are what set this page apart.
"Bể Nature suối đá" piles nouns together and reads a little stiff; "Bể Nature tái hiện suối đá" would read more naturally
"Nature" comes from the source title, not the page text. That's acceptable, but the text itself never names the style
"Bể Nature" mixes in the English style name. It matches the source's 'Nature Style' and the sibling titles, but a fully Vietnamese term would read more naturally.
It leaves out the swift-river-stone feel ('đá ở những con sông nước chảy xiết'), which is the page's most distinctive image.
"Ludwigia cam" shortens "Ludwigia pantanal ngọn cam"; it reads as if the whole plant is orange, but only the tips are
Names only 2 of the 5 colored plants (leaves out Bacopa, Barclaya, Ammania). That's acceptable, but the title leans on plant lists rather than the page's focus on contrast and layout
"chuẩn NBAT" is supported by the text, but readers who don't know the acronym get no context; it's slightly jargon-heavy
Title is long; it could be shorter without losing what makes it distinct
"Bể Dutch" mixes English into the title, but the page's text says "Bể Hà Lan". "Bể kiểu Hà Lan" would match the page better.
"với cây xếp bậc thang": the "với" structure reads a bit like a translation; something like "cây xếp bậc thang" without the linker, or "bố cục bậc thang", would read more naturally.
"Bể Dutch" uses the English loanword while the text says "kiểu Hà Lan". It's common slang among fishkeepers, but "bể kiểu Hà Lan" would match the text more closely.
still promises a count the text lacks: title promises 10; 6 headings, none numbered, lists of 3, 4
Starting with bare 'Loài cá' sounds stiff in Vietnamese; 'Những loài cá' or 'Các loài cá' would read more naturally.
Dropping the number means the title no longer gives a count, so it can't mislead, but readers lose a hint of what the list covers.

If you count each species, the text lists 10 (betta, corydoras, 4 schooling tetras/rasbora, rainbowfish, blood parrot, pleco, platy), so the original '10' may have been right. By section headings there are only 7.
still promises a count the text lacks: title promises 10; 7 headings, none numbered, lists of 5
The 8 matches the eight H2 sections, but several of them (new tank, cleanup crew, weekly maintenance) are fixes or FAQs rather than actual 'reasons', so 'lý do' fits only loosely
Two of the eight sections are both about CO2, which could be read as one reason
still promises a count the text lacks: title promises 10; 8 headings, none numbered, lists of 5
The 'xếp theo mức quan trọng' (ranked by importance) claim is kept from OLD, but nothing in the headings shows the tips are ranked.
Dropping the number fixes the overpromise: the text has about 25 bold-lead tips (4+2+4+6+4+2+3), not 28.
A specific count such as '25 mẹo' would also have fit, but leaving the number out is safer because the first section has no bullets.
